import MumfordLib.SingularChainGeneration
import MumfordLib.SingularSubdivisionEventualSmallness

/-!
# Eventual smallness of subdivided finite singular chains

The singular-simplex smallness theorem extends to every singular chain because
chains are finite linear combinations of simplex generators. Addition uses the
maximum of the two subdivision bounds, and scalar multiplication preserves the
bound.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

noncomputable section

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
open scoped Simplicial

namespace Mumford.Analytic

variable {X : TopCat} {n : ℕ}

/-- Every sufficiently high subdivision of a singular chain factors through
the chains subordinate to an open cover. -/
theorem singularChain_eventually_subdivision_small_factor
    {ι : Type*} (U : ι → Set X) (hopen : ∀ i, IsOpen (U i))
    (hcover : ∀ x : X, ∃ i, x ∈ U i)
    (c : ModuleCat.of ℤ ℤ ⟶ (IntegralSingularChainComplex X).X n) :
    ∃ K : ℕ, ∀ k ≥ K,
      ∃ d : ModuleCat.of ℤ ℤ ⟶ (IntegralSmallSingularChainComplex X U).X n,
        d ≫ (smallSingularChainInclusion X U).f n =
          c ≫ (End.of (singularSubdivision X n)) ^ k := by
  induction singularChain_mem_span c using Submodule.span_induction with
  | mem c hc =>
      obtain ⟨σ, rfl⟩ := hc
      exact singularSimplexChain_eventually_subdivision_small_factor U hopen hcover σ
  | zero =>
      exact ⟨0, fun _ _ => ⟨0, by simp⟩⟩
  | add a b ha hb ia ib =>
      obtain ⟨Ka, hKa⟩ := ia
      obtain ⟨Kb, hKb⟩ := ib
      refine ⟨max Ka Kb, fun k hk => ?_⟩
      obtain ⟨da, hda⟩ := hKa k ((le_max_left _ _).trans hk)
      obtain ⟨db, hdb⟩ := hKb k ((le_max_right _ _).trans hk)
      exact ⟨da + db, by simp only [Preadditive.add_comp, hda, hdb]⟩
  | smul r c hc ih =>
      obtain ⟨K, hK⟩ := ih
      refine ⟨K, fun k hk => ?_⟩
      obtain ⟨d, hd⟩ := hK k hk
      exact ⟨r • d, by simp only [Linear.smul_comp, hd]⟩

end Mumford.Analytic
